title: Vhal and the Sallow coast
caption: A salt-chart of the principal Vhaleni port and the five leagues of shore east of it, drawn in the tar-and-wet-rope manner of the Council's own surveyors: the Quay with its piers, crane, moored salt boats and the pulled benches; the Council room that smells of tar and wet rope, the tide-tally house and the glass furnaces within the town; the Salt Pans outside it with their dippers at dawn and their drying salt-paper; the blue-green Glaze Cliffs stained by old lead workings, and the glass-sand pits behind them; the silt-mouthed Ilm entering from the west and the Salt Road coming up from Greybank by the coast pass. In the sea the Sallow draw runs seaward against the wind, with a brine-gull, a salt boat and a salt-thing by report, and a surveyor's notes on boat-shares passing through mothers, contracts that rot in the damp, and children warned not to lick the cliffs. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with compass, league scale and a convention of signs.
